answer.evidence: The main body (rows 12-29) is a flat front view of vertical planks with dark seams. The top rows 12-13 are only slightly narrower (56 vs 64) and have no front-edge line or eave shadow. The one light line (row 18-21, #b89456) is a rope band that runs diagonally across the face, so it is not a top edge. The rope at rows 1-7 is a thin strip with no top surface. The posts and the gray stone end blocks are vertical faces with no visible horizontal surface. No ellipse, roof or visible contents show a top, so this is a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The references are whole houses (tiled roof, timber or stone walls, door), while the candidate is a small plank bridge with two grey end posts and a rope rail, so the kind does not match. Judged by eye against the references' material ramps: the planks show about 3-4 wood tones with a few grain lines, and the stone posts are nearly flat grey blocks with little per-stone shading. The references have 5-6 steps per material, per-tile roof highlights and speckled plaster. The measured visible tones per tile (12) equal reference h101 (12) and are close to h112 (10), but only 20 distinct colours in total, against 185 and 66, shows a much thinner palette. Near-flat coverage is 11% against 0% for both references, which fits the flat post faces. The dark edge pixels are 44% neutral, against 7-9% for the references, so the outline is part neutral black and part tinted, which reads as 'mixed' and leans towards the sticker look. The piece is clean and readable but shallower than the Beodeul standard.

The rope rail is a thin two-tone line, and the grey stone end posts are close to flat blocks with only 2-3 tones. The measured facts are mixed. The candidate has 12 visible tones per tile, equal to h101 (12) and above h112 (10).
